name: Canberra Times cryptic crossword, Saturday 5 December 1970

clue.text: Entrechats at the bar?

blocks.note: surface reading: ballet leaps in which the dancer beats the feet together, practised at the barre
setter's reading: the dregs left in the bottom of glasses in a pub, punning on the feet tapping in a ballet step

explanation.surface: A dancer practising leaps at the ballet barre.
explanation.walkthrough: Split HEEL TAPS and it describes the dancer's feet; as one word it is the last drop of liquor left in a glass at the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Heeltaps are the small remnants of drink left undrunk at the bottom of a glass, found in a bar.

clue.text: Jill's greeting to pirate?

blocks.note: a casual hello
Jack is Jill's partner in the nursery rhyme, the one she would greet

explanation.surface: Jill from the nursery rhyme calls out a hello to a buccaneer.
explanation.walkthrough: Jill would naturally say 'Hi, Jack' to her companion from the rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: To pirate a vessel or aircraft is to seize it by force, which is exactly what hijacking means as a verb.

clue.text: The attempt of James Cook

definitions.note: stands for the ship of James Cook

blocks.note: first meaning: an effort or try
second meaning: the name of the ship Captain Cook sailed to Australia

explanation.surface: Captain Cook's great effort at exploration.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain James Cook's ship on his first Pacific voyage, when he charted eastern Australia, was HMS Endeavour.
explanation.definitionFit: An endeavour is an earnest effort, and Endeavour was also the vessel Cook commanded on his 1768 voyage.

clue.text: Old English watchman

blocks.note: surface reading: a night watchman or guard from England's past
setter's reading: a man who made watches, a famous English clockmaker of the seventeenth century

explanation.surface: A guard patrolling the streets of old England.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Tompion (1639-1713) was the celebrated 'father of English clockmaking'; his name came to mean one of his watches.
explanation.definitionFit: Tompion was an English maker of clocks and watches from the Stuart era, so literally a watch man.

clue.text: Reward for the honest turner

blocks.note: surface reading: a trustworthy craftsman who works a lathe
setter's reading: an idiom about turning a coin, meaning to earn money by fair work, so the honest turner earns a small coin

explanation.surface: Wages paid to a reliable lathe worker.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom is 'turn an honest penny': whoever does that is an honest turner, and what they gain is the coin itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A small coin is what is earned in the phrase about making money by fair work, so it is the turner's pay.

clue.text: A chicken from Italy has a team to beat the jumping cow

definitions.note: the mission that reached the moon, beating the cow from the nursery rhyme

blocks.note: taken as written
the Italian word for chicken
a cricket or football side has that many players

explanation.surface: An Italian chicken joins a team to outdo a leaping cow.
explanation.walkthrough: In 'Hey Diddle Diddle' the cow jumped over the moon; the 1969 Apollo 11 mission actually landed there.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1969 American spaceflight landed people on the lunar surface, outdoing the nursery-rhyme cow that merely leapt over it.

clue.text: Ancient writer's reed

definitions.note: stands for the ancient writer's material

blocks.note: first meaning: the paper of the ancient Egyptians and Greeks
second meaning: the tall water plant from which that paper was made

explanation.surface: The reed pen an ancient scribe wrote with.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a reed pen, but the plant and the writing sheet share one name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nile sedge gave its name to the sheets ancient scribes wrote on, made from its pressed stems.

clue.text: Though notedly slow, many take the old ship

blocks.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a large number
the ship of Jason and the Argonauts in Greek myth

explanation.surface: Many people board an old ship despite its sluggish pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notedly' means in musical notation: the answer is a tempo marking.
explanation.definitionFit: As a musical direction the Italian term instructs players to perform in a broad, very unhurried tempo.

clue.text: Weekend watchman

blocks.note: surface reading: a guard who works Saturday and Sunday shifts
setter's reading: a British Sunday newspaper whose name also means someone who watches

explanation.surface: A security guard on duty at the weekend.
explanation.walkthrough: The Observer is the long-running British Sunday newspaper, so it appears only at the weekend.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who watches is a looker-on, and the title of a London Sunday paper carries the same name.

clue.text: Eagle's brain

blocks.note: surface reading: the brain of a bird of prey
setter's reading: Eagle was the Apollo 11 lunar module, whose guidance was run by an electronic machine

explanation.surface: The mind of a bird of prey.
explanation.walkthrough: Eagle was the lunar module that landed on the moon in 1969; its guidance machine was its brain.
explanation.definitionFit: An electronic calculating machine acts as the thinking organ of a spacecraft, steering and guiding its landing.

clue.text: Capital decision in the Golden Apple Stakes

definitions.text: Capital decision in the Golden Apple Stakes

blocks.note: surface reading: an excellent ruling, or one made in a capital city
setter's reading: the Greek myth in which a Trojan prince awarded a golden apple to the fairest goddess

explanation.surface: A race steward's verdict in a horse race called the Golden Apple Stakes.
explanation.walkthrough: In myth the Trojan prince Paris gave the golden apple to Aphrodite over Hera and Athena; Paris is also a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical contest among three goddesses was settled by a Trojan prince, whose name matches the French capital.

clue.text: Beginner at home is cautious about it

indicators.note: about means around, so one word wraps itself round the other

blocks.note: chary means wary or careful
taken as written

explanation.surface: A novice at home is careful about something.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the proverb 'charity begins at home'.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says generosity to others starts within the household, so this virtue is what begins there.

clue.text: Room for tricks and games

blocks.note: surface reading: a games room or playroom
setter's reading: the room that is part of two set phrases for simple home entertainment

explanation.surface: A playroom where tricks and games happen.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer completes both 'parlour tricks' and 'parlour games'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitting room in an older house is where party amusements were played, hence the stock phrases for them.

clue.text: High degree of reporting from 5, 27 on this

definitions.text: High degree of reporting from 5, 27 on this

blocks.note: surface reading: journalism of a lofty standard
setter's reading: the 1969 mission's launch to the lunar surface, from which astronauts reported back

explanation.surface: Top-quality news coverage of the famous 1969 mission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High' is literal: the reporting came from very high up, sent back during the launch to the moon.
explanation.definitionFit: A launch of a spacecraft aimed at the lunar surface is the kind of mission the earlier answer flew.

clue.text: Cutting Grub Street aphorisms?

definitions.note: the adjective names what the tools do rather than the tools themselves; the question mark flags this loose, functional definition

blocks.note: Grub Street was the London street of poor hack writers, so it stands for a hack, and the possessive is implied
a saw is an old saying

explanation.surface: Sharp, biting sayings from cheap writers.
explanation.walkthrough: Grub Street was a London street of struggling hack writers, and the name came to stand for them; 'saws' are proverbs.
explanation.definitionFit: These fine-toothed tools in a frame are used for sawing through metal, so they do the cutting.

clue.text: A possible cause of impudence

indicators.note: possible suggests just one of several potential versions, so the letters may be rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something that might lead to cheekiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauce is informal British slang for cheek or insolence, as in 'none of your sauce'.

clue.text: "Dear Child! ... If thou appear - by solemn thought" (Wordsworth)

definitions.text: "Dear Child! ... If thou appear - by solemn thought" (Wordsworth)

blocks.clueFragment: "Dear Child! ... If thou appear - by solemn thought"
blocks.note: surface reading: a quotation from a Wordsworth sonnet with a word left blank
setter's reading: the missing word from the sonnet 'It is a beauteous evening, calm and free'

explanation.walkthrough: The sonnet 'It is a beauteous evening' reads 'Dear Child! dear Girl! that walkest with me here, / If thou appear untouched by solemn thought'.
explanation.definitionFit: The poet's word means unaffected or unmoved, describing the girl seemingly unmoved by solemn reflection.

clue.text: A golf-ball on snow is innocently deceptive

definitions.note: an adjective phrase for a noun answer: something innocently deceptive

blocks.note: first meaning: in golf a ball's lie is where it rests, and on snow that resting place is pale
second meaning: a harmless untruth told to be kind

explanation.surface: A golf ball resting on snow is hard to see.
explanation.walkthrough: A ball's 'lie' in golf is the spot where it comes to rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A harmless fib told to spare feelings is the classic small untruth meant to mislead without malice.

clue.text: The eminence in Fen church Or Ebury Street

indicators.note: in says the wanted letters sit inside the words that follow

blocks.note: surface padding, outside the hidden letters
found running across the words
surface padding, outside the hidden letters

explanation.surface: A notable figure at a Fenland church or on Ebury Street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eminence' tempts as a cardinal's title, but here it means a high place; Ebury Street is in London's Belgravia.
explanation.definitionFit: Horeb is the biblical mountain where Moses received the law, and an eminence is a hill or summit.

clue.text: Liberal if unconventional type

indicators.note: unconventional means not in the usual order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A broad-minded but unorthodox sort of person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Type' looks like a kind of person; it is printing type.
explanation.definitionFit: This system of raised dots is a form of printed lettering read by touch, so it counts as a kind of type.

clue.text: Blimey, a horse-doctor in the Navy? So we hear

definitions.note: stands for a vessel in the Navy

indicators.note: we hear points to what the words sound like when spoken

blocks.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise like blimey, and a vet treats horses

explanation.surface: Surprise that a horse vet serves with the Navy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cor!' and 'Blimey!' are both British exclamations of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: A corvette is a small, fast warship used by navies for escort and anti-submarine duty.

clue.text: In the first place read, next remember, and last this

indicators.note: read what is in the first place means take letters from inside the words given

blocks.note: found running across the two words

explanation.surface: Instructions to read first, remember next, and do this last.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a list of steps, but the answer sits inside 'next remember'.
explanation.definitionFit: The outermost or final item in a series is the farthest one, the one at the very end.

clue.text: His place of retirement is up on the hill - to avoid the duns?

definitions.note: points to the person hiding from the duns

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from bottom to top, backwards

blocks.note: where one retires for the night
a tor is a rocky hill on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A man retreats to a hilltop to dodge his creditors.
explanation.walkthrough: Duns are people demanding payment of debts.
explanation.definitionFit: One who owes money is the person creditors pursue and who therefore tries to hide from them.

clue.text: That's going round about showing mailed fists

definitions.note: stands for the shows of mailed fists

indicators.note: going round means encircling, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
re means concerning, as in letter headings

explanation.surface: That is what goes round when people show armoured fists.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'mailed fist' is a show of force, from armoured gauntlets.
explanation.definitionFit: Displays of the iron hand are warnings of force to come, which is what intimidating declarations are.

clue.text: Early heart transplant?

indicators.note: a transplant moves things to new places, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An organ transplant performed in its early days.
explanation.walkthrough: Rathe is an archaic and poetic word, as in Milton's 'rathe primrose'.
explanation.definitionFit: An old poetic adjective meaning coming before its time or soon in the season, as with blossoms.

clue.text: Jo's sister goes to a French town

blocks.note: in Little Women, Jo March's sisters are Meg, Beth and Amy
the French word for a, feminine

explanation.surface: Jo March's sister travels to a town in France.
explanation.walkthrough: Béthune is a town in the Pas-de-Calais in northern France.
explanation.definitionFit: Béthune is a market town in northern France, near Lille, in the Pas-de-Calais department.

clue.text: Audible disapproval of the demon rum

indicators.note: audible means heard, so go by the sound of the following word

blocks.note: jeers from a crowd

explanation.surface: Temperance campaigners loudly decrying the evils of rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The demon rum' is the temperance movement's phrase for alcohol in general.
explanation.definitionFit: The temperance phrase names strong drink in general, and the informal word for alcoholic drink is a match.

clue.text: No elopement by the singer from this her humble home

definitions.text: No elopement by the singer from this her humble home

blocks.note: surface reading: a singer who refuses to run away with her lover
setter's reading: the popular song in which the singer would not leave her simple dwelling

explanation.surface: A singer declines to run off and leave her modest home.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the title phrase of an old popular song about a girl content in her simple home.
explanation.definitionFit: A small timber shack is a humble dwelling, the modest home in the song the singer refuses to leave.

clue.text: See 5
Though withstanding attack he has to yield about the end

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: to defer is to give way to someone
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man resisting assault must eventually give in near the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: The paradox of a resister who yields is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: The player or soldier who resists an assault is the one guarding against it, protecting a position.
